text: . Youth Affairs and Sports Minister Dr. Mansukh Mandaviya has called for greater transparency in athlete selection, athlete-centric governance and institutional reforms in the country’s sports ecosystem. Addressing the National Sports Federation Conclave 2026 in New Delhi today, Dr. Mandaviya said, the interests and welfare of athletes must remain the foremost priority for all stakeholders. He stressed that no athlete should ever face injustice.The Minister called for complete transparency in selection trials, saying open trials should be recorded on camera in the presence of observers to ensure fairness and accountability.On doping, Dr. Mandaviya called for a comprehensive strategy to eliminate the menace from Indian sports. He said, action should not be limited to athletes and that the entire chain, including manufacturers, suppliers, facilitators and users, must be dealt with through a transparent and robust mechanism.The Minister also stressed the need to strengthen India’s indigenous coaching ecosystem and reduce overdependence on foreign coaches. The conclave reviewed the compliance of National Sports Federations with the National Sports Governance Act, 2025, good governance practices and India’s preparedness for the Asian Games 2026, Los Angeles Olympics 2028 and Commonwealth Games 2030.

. Union Minister of Electronics and Information Technology Ashwini Vaishnaw has said that the Government is cognizant of the risks associated with children’s online activities, including exposure to harmful content, cyberbullying, online exploitation and digital addiction.In a written reply to a question in Lok Sabha today, Mr Vaishnaw said that the Government keeps itself informed of global developments and evolving international regulatory approaches relating to online safety, including measures adopted by different jurisdictions for protection of children in the digital environment. He said that the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 (DPDP Act) has been enacted, which establishes the legal framework to regulate the processing of digital personal data.The DPDP Act provides a legal framework for safeguarding children’s privacy online. Mr Vaishnaw said that the Ministry is implementing a project on Information Security Education and Awareness for generating human resources in Information Security and creating general awareness on various aspects of cyber hygiene & cyber security among the masses.

. India’s capital markets remained resilient during the financial year 2025-26 despite global uncertainties, with India retaining the top position globally in the number of Initial Public Offerings (IPO) and ranking third in funds raised.According to SEBI’s Annual Report released yesterday, the regulator said, the primary equity market remained strong even as corporate bond mobilisation declined by 8.4 per cent to 9.1 lakh crore rupees, marking the first fall in four years. Public debt issuances, however, rose nearly 39 per cent, while municipal bond fundraising surged to one thousand 756 crore rupees through 14 issues.SEBI also introduced a new Closing Auction Session (CAS) to improve price discovery and align India’s markets with global standards. The report noted that foreign portfolio investor (FPI) ownership fell to a 15-year low, while domestic institutional investors (DII) reached a record 17 per cent equity holding by March 2026.Mutual fund participation continued to expand, driven largely by Tier-3 cities, with monthly SIP contributions touching a record average of over 16,400 crore rupees. It also said, 62 per cent of retail investors are influenced by financial influencers on social media, prompting stronger investor protection measures.The regulator outlined several initiatives for the coming year, including Project Jagrook for investor awareness, an AI-enabled WhatsApp campaign, simplified nomination norms, a fast-track mechanism for alternative investment funds, the SEBI Setu portal, and a pilot project for tokenisation of corporate bonds using distributed ledger technology.

. Minister of Tourism and Culture Gajendra Singh Shekhawat today said that cinema is more than entertainment; it is a bridge to culture, heritage and tourism. He said this during a fireside chat with Netflix Co-CEO Ted Sarandos in New Delhi. Mr Shekhawat highlighted that every Indian story has the potential to inspire someone, somewhere in the world, to experience India. The Minister said that India’s ancient civilisation and cultural diversity are its greatest strengths, and platforms like Netflix can play a key role in taking India’s stories and soft power to global audiences. He noted that the ministry’s partnership with Netflix, including the As Seen on Netflix integration on the Incredible India portal, reflects the shared vision of showcasing India’s rich cultural diversity and strengthening its global soft power through authentic storytelling. Mr Shekhawat also stressed that the Centre is working with all stakeholders to provide tourists with a seamless travel experience across the country.On the sidelines of the fireside chat, talking to Akashvani News, Mr  Shekhawat said that the Ministry’s partnerships with platforms such as Netflix, YouTube, Google, and airline companies including IndiGo and Air India are based on non-commercial and mutually beneficial agreements, without financial payments by the government to these companies.He said that these collaborations will promote India’s tourism globally by showcasing the country’s destinations and cultural diversity. The Minister highlighted that visual storytelling plays a crucial role in influencing travellers’ decisions.

. In Badminton, India’s Tanvi Sharma, Ashmita Chaliha and Rakshitha Ramraj have progressed to the Women singles quarterfinals at the Korea Masters in Asan. Tanvi continued her impressive run by defeating her compatriot Shriyanshi Valishetty 21-16, 17-21, 21-13 in the pre-quarterfinals. Ashmita beat home favourite Kim Min-ji 21-17, 21-6, while Rakshitha defeated Japan’s Manami Suizu 22-20, 21-10. However, Anmol Kharb’s, Isharani Baruah’s and Mansi Singh’s Korea Masters campaign came to an end in the pre-quarterfinals.In the men’s doubles pre-quarterfinals, the Indian duo of Prithvi Krishnamurthy Roy and Krishna Prasad Garaga defeated a South Korean pair to secure a place in the quarterfinals. All eyes will now be on tomorrow’s women’s singles and men’s doubles quarterfinal matches.

. In Badminton, Indian shuttlers Rakshitha Ramraj and Ashmita Chaliha have entered the women’s singles semi-finals of the Korea Masters in Asan. Rakshitha defeated compatriot Tanvi Sharma 18-21, 21-19, 21-18 in the quarterfinal match today. Ashmita advanced to the semi-final after stunning top seed Hina Akechi 20-22, 21-15, 21-19. Ashmita and Rakshitha will face each other in the semifinal tomorrow.Meanwhile, India’s men’s doubles campaign came to an end after Pruthvi Krishnamurthy Roy and Krishna Prasad Garaga lost to the Malaysian duo of Man Wei Chong and Soh Wooi Yik in the quarter final.

. The government has said that more than one crore 73  lakh e-Passports have been issued so far in India and abroad. In a written reply in Rajya Sabha today, Minister of State for External Affairs Kirti Vardhan Singh said that currently, all Regional Passport Offices, Passport Seva Kendras and Post Office Passport Seva Kendras in India and all the Indian Missions abroad are issuing e-Passports. He informed that the e-Passport was launched in May last year. Mr Singh said that the Passport Seva Programme provided comprehensive digital platforms. This includes the Passport Seva Portal, Passport Seva Mobile Apps and a centralised citizen service call centre, enabling applicants to access information, track application status and obtain responses to routine queries without visiting Regional Passport Offices. The Minister said, these digital initiatives have substantially reduced the need for physical visits for administrative enquiries while improving accessibility, convenience and service delivery.

. The National Health Authority’s Scan and Share service under Ayushman Bharat Digital Mission has crossed the landmark milestone of 25 Crore OPD registrations. The Ministry of Health and Family Welfare said that the milestone underscores the rapid scale-up of citizen-centric digital services under the Mission and reflects the increasing adoption of ABHA-enabled digital health solutions across the country.The Ministry said, since its launch in October 2022, the Scan and Share service has transformed the OPD registration experience by enabling patients to complete hospital registration digitally through a simple QR-code scan. The Ministry said that the service is currently operational across 30 thousand 800 healthcare facilities spanning 36 States and Union Territories and 756 districts across the country. Of them, over 24 thousand are public healthcare facilities and 6,481 are private healthcare facilities.The Ministry added that on average, nearly four lakh patients use the Scan and Register service every day for OPD registration, reflecting the growing trust of citizens in digital healthcare services. It added that among the States and Union Territories, Bihar leads the country with over 7.30 crore Scan and Register transactions, followed by Uttar Pradesh with 4.09 crore, Andhra Pradesh with 3.38 crore and Jammu and Kashmir with 1.39 crore Scan and Register transactions.Among Government healthcare facilities, AIIMS New Delhi has generated the highest number of Scan and Register registrations with over 54.29 lakh registrations. Speaking on the achievement, Dr. Sunil Kumar Barnwal, Chief Executive Officer, National Health Authority, said, crossing the milestone of 25 crore OPD registrations through Scan and Register reflects the growing trust that citizens and healthcare providers have placed in India’s digital health ecosystem.

. External Affairs Minister Dr. S Jaishankar today said that India’s relations with Pakistan can only move ahead in an environment free of terror, hostility and violence. In a written reply in Lok Sabha, Dr Jaishankar said that Pakistan continues to follow the policy of cross-border terrorism and using terrorism as an instrument of state policy against India.The Minister said that India withdrew Most Favoured Nation (MFN) Status to Pakistan, and hiked customs duty on all goods originating in or exported from Pakistan to 200 percent after the Pulwama terror attack. India took a number of diplomatic steps, including holding Indus Waters Treaty in abeyance, closing Attari check-post, restricting visas, and downsizing diplomatic and official presence at the respective Missions following Pulwama terror attack. Dr Jaishankar stated that military action targeting terrorist infrastructure in Pakistan and Pakistan-occupied Jammu and Kashmir was also undertaken.The External Affairs Minister informed that at present, India and Pakistan maintain their respective diplomatic Missions in each other’s capital. Both sides continue to have functional engagements, including DGMO-level talks, exchange of pre-notification of flight testing of ballistic missiles, exchange of list of nuclear installations, and exchange of list of prisoners in each other’s custody.

. Rain warnings continue in all districts of Keralam today as well. An orange alert has been issued in seven districts. Akashvani correspondent reports that rain warnings have continued in all districts of the state for more than seven days. Today, orange alert, indicating the possibility of isolated very heavy rainfall, has been declared in the Kasaragod, Kannur, Wayanad, Kozhikode, Kottayam, Alappuzha and Pathanamthitta districts. A yellow alert is in force in all the other districts. Winds with speeds of up to 50 kilometres per hour are also likely in Keralam and Lakshadweep. Moderate rainfall has been occurring across all districts of the state since midnight.

. India will host the first Global South Film Festival next year. It was announced today at a press conference held on the sidelines of the BRICS WAVES Bazaar in Mumbai. Several agreements aimed at strengthening international cooperation in the film and entertainment sector were also announced.Organisations including the National Film Development Corporation (NFDC) and the National Film Archive of India (NFAI) signed agreements, exchanged Letters of Intent and held talks with partner institutions from countries including Brazil, Russia and Vietnam. The participating organisations also agreed to explore opportunities for film co-production.The two-day WAVES BRICS Bazaar, which opened in Mumbai yesterday, concludes this evening. Prakash Magdum, Managing Director of the NFDC, said the initiative brought together more than 900 delegates from the 20 BRICS member and partner countries. Around 250 meetings were held during the one-and-a-half-day event, providing a platform for government agencies, entertainment industry professionals, investors and content creators to exchange ideas and explore opportunities for collaboration.

. External Affairs Minister Dr S Jaishankar has said, India stands for inclusive, demand-driven development cooperation with Africa that enhances local capacity to support national priorities.Speaking on the occasion of Africa Day in New Delhi yesterday, Dr Jaishankar noted that India is proud to be one of Africa’s largest trade and investment partners and the bilateral trade between the two nations stood at 93 billion last year. He added that India has also emerged as one of the top investors in Africa, with cumulative investments exceeding 80 billion dollar.Dr Jaishankar said, India’s approach to Africa is guided by the ten principles outlined by Prime Minister Narendra Modi during his address to the Ugandan Parliament in 2018. He added these principles enshrine Africa among the top priorities of India with engagements through demand driven development partnerships, open markets for trade and investment, digital revolution for Africa’s development.The External Affairs Minister stressed that India’s enduring commitment to the Global South and the African Continent is reflected in the inclusion of the African Union as a permanent member of G20 during India’s presidency.

. In United Kingdom, Members of the British Kashmiri diaspora staged a demonstration in Bradford yesterday, expressing solidarity with the people of Pakistan-occupied Jammu and Kashmir (PoJK) and voicing support for the demands of the Joint Awami Action Committee (JAAC).Protesters gathered in the city centre carrying banners and placards, calling for the protection of fundamental rights, civil liberties and human dignity. Organisers said, the rally was aimed at drawing international attention to what they described as the deteriorating human rights situation in PoJK. Speakers at the demonstration alleged that security operations carried out over the past two months had resulted in civilian casualties, widespread fear and restrictions affecting local communities. They also claimed that women, children and elderly residents had been among those adversely affected. Participants called for transparent and impartial investigations into allegations of excessive use of force, house raids and other reported human rights violations. They urged the authorities to ensure accountability and uphold the rule of law.The demonstrators also appealed to the international community, human rights organisations and the British government to closely monitor developments in PoJK and support efforts to protect fundamental freedoms and promote a peaceful resolution to the issues raised by local communities.

. Iran and Oman have reached an understanding  to reopen the Strait of Hormuz for 60 days. According to the local media reports, the agreement, which still needs approval by Iran’s Supreme National Security Council and could be announced within days, aims to resume navigation in the waterway. Vessels entering the strait will use a route close to Iran, while those leaving will take one close to Oman. According to sources, no transit fees or service charges will be imposed, and regional parties may participate in demining and technical procedures.Following the agreement’s approval, the United States and Iran will return to their peace memorandum of understanding (MoU) and working in proposal on reopening and safe navigation of commercial shipping through the strait. Iran tightened its grip on the strait on Feb. 28, barring safe passage of vessels belonging to or affiliated with Israel and the United States following their joint strikes on Iranian territory.In June, Iran and the United States signed the MoU on ending the war on all fronts, including Lebanon. The two sides were scheduled to hold negotiations within a 60-day period to reach a final agreement, but recent escalation in the region has left the talks’ fate uncertain.

. Former champion PV Sindhu will be the ninth seed in the women’s singles event at the BWF World Badminton Championships 2026, scheduled to be held at the Indira Gandhi Indoor Stadium in New Delhi from August 17 to 23. India’s highest-seeded entry at the World Badminton Championships will be the men’s doubles pair of Satwiksairaj Rankireddy and Chirag Shetty, who have been handed the fifth seed. Former world championships bronze medallist Lakshya Sen is seeded 14th in men’s singles, while Dhruv Kapila and Olympian Tanisha Crasto are the 15th seeds in mixed doubles. India will have two entries in each of the five badminton disciplines at the home world championships, with at least one seeded contender in four of them.

. The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has forecast heavy to very heavy rainfall over East Rajasthan and Odisha today. The Met Department also predicted heavy rainfall over Himachal Pradesh, Uttarakhand, East Uttar Pradesh, West Rajasthan, East Madhya Pradesh, Jharkhand, Chhattisgarh, Konkan, Goa, Coastal Andhra Pradesh, Kerala, Mahe and some parts of Northeast India. According to IMD, thunderstorms accompanied by lightning and gusts are expected to prevail over Lakshadweep, North Interior Karnataka, Tamil Nadu, Puducherry and Karaikal today.

. Union Home and Cooperation Minister Amit Shah will inaugurate the new office of the National Urban Co-operative Finance and Development Corporation Limited (NUCFDC) today in Mumbai. The Home Minister will also interact with representatives of State Urban Cooperative Bank Federations and district associations of Maharashtra. During the programme, a Memorandum of Understanding will be exchanged between NUCFDC and the National Forensic Sciences University.The collaboration will play an important role in strengthening cybersecurity, technological capabilities, and institutional capacity in the Urban Cooperative Banking sector. Mr Shah will later attend the BSE International Convention Centre, alongside Maharashtra Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis. He will also inaugurate a Security Operations Centre (SOC) to strengthen the cybersecurity of Urban Cooperative Banks.

. Hockey India today announced the 18-member Indian junior women’s team for the AHF Junior Asia Cup 2026, to be held in Moqi, China, from August 30 to September 13.The squad comprises 18 players along with two alternate players and will be led by midfielder Khaidem Shileima Chanu. The team heads into the tournament after an extensive training camp under newly appointed head coach Tim White, who took charge earlier this year.The tournament will bring together the continent’s leading junior teams, serving as a key platform for the next generation of Asian hockey talent. The match schedule and pool compositions will be announced closer to the start of the tournament.

. Arunachal’s para shuttler Biri Takar has clinched Double Medal at BWF Para World Circuit in Brazil. Takar has won Gold in Men’s Doubles and Bronze in Men’s Singles. Arunachal Pradesh Chief Minister Pema Khandu congratulated the sportsman for his international achievements.Congratulating the athlete, Chief Minister in a social media post highlighted that Takar is a beneficiary of the Chief Minister’s Award to Champion Excellence in Sports (CM ACES) programme.  and said his international success reflects the programme growing impact on nurturing sporting talent in the state.
. In the Indian bullion market, 24 carat gold was trading 0.4 percent up at 1,49,340 rupees per 10 grams, while silver was trading 0.6 percent down at 2,27,030 rupees per kilogram, a short while ago.

. The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) said, credit extended by Non-Banking Financial Companies (NBFCs) grew by 14.4 per cent year-on-year in June 2026, compared to 11.1 per cent a year earlier.According to the RBI, credit to agriculture and allied activities rose 17.9 per cent, up from 5.1 per cent a year ago. Retail loan growth accelerated to 20.3 per cent from 14.3 per cent, driven by strong growth in housing, vehicle loans and loans against gold jewellery. However, credit growth to the services sector moderated to 17.6 per cent from 22.4 percent, while lending to industry slowed to 6.7 percent from 10.3 percent, mainly due to subdued growth in infrastructure lending.

. Indian grandmaster R. Praggnanandhaa has clinched the Grand Chess Tour St. Louis Rapid and Blitz title in the United States. The 20-year-old secured the championship after drawing against Uzbekistan’s Grandmaster Javokhir Sindarov in the penultimate round, finishing the tournament with 23 points out of a possible 35.Praggnanandhaa maintained the lead throughout the five-day event, with  Sindarov mounted a strong challenge in the final stages but fell short, finishing runner-up with a 1.5-point deficit.Earlier in June, Praggnanandhaa scripted history by claiming the Norway Chess 2026 crown in Oslo after defeating Germany’s Vincent Keymer in the tenth and final round.

. India’s foreign exchange reserves rose by 10.5 billion US dollars (USD) to 692.8 billion US dollars during the week ended July 31. According to the Reserve Bank of India data, Foreign currency assets, the largest component of the reserves, increased by 8.7 billion USD to 564.6 billion USD during the week. Gold reserves added 1.6 billion USD to 104.7 billion US dollars. Special Drawing Rights increased by 48 million USD to 18.66 billion USD. Country’s reserve position with the International Monetary Fund was up by 28 million USD to around 4.8 billion USD.

. In the Asian markets, South Korea’s Kospi index dropped 0.6 per cent, and Japan’s Nikkei 225 dipped 0.1 per cent. Major European indices were trading on a positive note today. Germany’s DAX added over 0.8 per cent, while London’s FTSE 100 rose more than 0.7 per cent, when reports last came in.

. In Thailand, a 14-year-old student shot and killed seven people in Nonthaburi province northwest of Bangkok. According to the officials, the shooter killed five staff members at a high school before taking his own life. The shooter also killed his two grandparents at their home prior to the school attack.Deputy Interior Minister Polapee Suwunchwee said, the shooting occurred at Debsirin Nonthaburi School in Nonthaburi province. Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul confirmed the shooter’s age and said the boy, who lived with his grandparents, had exhibited stress related to school. Police said the small, compact weapon used in the attack was legally registered to the kid’s grandfather. Bangyai Hospital reported that 23 people were injured, with 10 in critical condition, primarily from gunshot wounds.

. The Government has said that the National Consumer Helpline (NCH) administered by the Department of Consumer Affairs has emerged as a single point of access to consumers across the country for their grievance redressal at a pre-litigation stage. In a written reply in Lok Sabha today, Minister of State for Consumer Affairs, Food and Public Distribution B L Verma said that consumers can register their grievances from all over the country in 17 languages through a toll-free number 1915.The Minister also said that 1,853 companies, who have voluntarily partnered with NCH, as part of the ‘Convergence’ programme directly respond to these grievances according to their redressal process and revert by providing a feedback to the complainant on the portal. Mr Verma also informed that NCH has successfully facilitated refunds amounting to over 91 crore rupees (including over 63 Crore rupees with regard to the grievances pertaining to e-commerce sector) to consumers between 25th April 2025 and 30th June 2026 by effectively addressing over 1,47,000 consumer grievances related to refund claims at the pre-litigation stage.

. The Government today said that it has strengthened the legal and institutional framework to deal with online piracy of cinematograph films, including unauthorized dissemination of films through intermediaries such as Telegram. In a written reply in Lok Sabha today, Minister of State for Information and Broadcasting Dr. L Murugan said, the Cinematograph Act, 1952 was amended through the Cinematograph (Amendment) Act, 2023 to introduce specific provisions to curb unauthorized recording and exhibition of films. The Minister also said that the newly inserted Section 7(1B)(ii) empowers the Government, under Section 79(3) of the Information Technology Act, 2000, to take action against intermediaries hosting pirated content. Mr. Murugan informed that under the Information Technology Rules, 2021, the intermediaries are required to remove any content violative of any law for the time being in force as and when brought to their knowledge either through a court order or through a notice by appropriate government or its authorized agency.

. A high-level bilateral meeting between India and Bhutan on cooperation in trans-border rivers was held in New Delhi today. The Indian delegation was led by Union Minister of Jal Shakti, C R Patil, while the Bhutanese delegation was headed by Minister for Energy and Natural Resources  Lyonpo Gem Tshering. The two sides reviewed the ongoing cooperation in the water resources sector, with focus on trans-border river management, flood forecasting and management, and hydrological data sharing. The two sides also reviewed the progress of the Punatsangchhu-I Hydroelectric Project in Bhutan, being implemented in partnership with the Indian government, and discussed measures for its expeditious completion.The delegations also discussed proposals to upgrade and strengthen Bhutan’s existing hydro-meteorological network and expand cooperation under the existing mechanism for sharing hydrological data on trans-border rivers. Both sides reaffirmed their commitment to the sustainable and mutually beneficial management of trans-boundary water resources and agreed to deepen cooperation through sustained technical collaboration, mutual trust and regular institutional engagement.

. Bangladesh’s Election Commission today announced that presidential election will be held on 20th of this month. The  elections were necessitated after Mohammed Shahabuddin resigned from the post on July 24, two years ahead of the end of his tenure. According to the schedule, nomination papers must be submitted at the office of the Chief Election Commissioner between 10 am and 4 pm on August 13. The scrutiny of nomination papers will be held on August 16. The last date for withdrawal of candidature is August 18.Mohammed Shahabuddin, a 1971 Liberation War veteran and former lower judiciary judge, had taken the oath in April 2023 for a five-year term. He cited health complications as the reason for his resignation.

. In a significant initiative to encourage and promote emerging filmmaking talent from the Union Territory of Jammu and Kashmir, the Department of Information and Public Relations (DIPR) has announced the IFFJK Emerging Filmmakers Competition 2026, as part of the scheduled 1st International Film Festival of Jammu & Kashmir (IFFJK). Registrations for the competition has commenced from today. Akashvani Jammu Correspondent reports that the competition is exclusively open to aspiring filmmakers from J&K and aims to provide a prestigious platform for young storytellers to showcase their creativity, cinematic vision and technical skills through original short films.The aspiring and emerging filmmakers are invited to submit original short films with a maximum duration of five minutes and the last date for submission is August 26. The applicants must be between 18 and 39 years of age as on September 1, 2026, and possess a valid domicile certificate of J&K. The competition is being organised around the theme “Rang-e-Cinema: Frames of a New Jammu & Kashmir”, reflecting the evolving cultural, social and creative narratives of the region while encouraging youth to present compelling stories through the medium of cinema. Interested filmmakers and cinematographers are advised to register by visiting the official IFFJK website www.iffjk.org and the detailed guidelines, eligibility criteria and the registration process are also available on this website for ease of aspirants. DIPR urges aspiring filmmakers from across J&K to seize this opportunity and contribute towards strengthening the Union Territory’s growing film culture through innovative and impactful storytelling.

. Prime Minister Narendra Modi will address the 57th convocation ceremony of the Indian Institute of Technology (IIT) Delhi today. He will address over 3 thousand graduating students, including 587 PhD scholars who will be conferred their degrees during the ceremony.Akashvani correspondent reports that Prime Minister Narendra Modi will present the Institute’s most prestigious honours, including the President’s Gold Medal, Director’s Gold Medal, Shankar Dayal Sharma Gold Medal and Perfect Ten Gold Medals, to the meritorious students during the ceremony.Further, Mr Modi will also inaugurate Param Pragya, an AI-powered high-performance supercomputing facility established at the Sonipat Campus of IIT Delhi. The state-of-the-art facility is expected to significantly enhance the institute’s capabilities in AI, data science, advanced computing, and interdisciplinary research. In a social media post, the Prime Minister has said that IIT Delhi has always made a rich contribution in the fields of research and innovation. Mr Modi said that he looks forward to being among the students and teachers of this pioneering institution.

. India’s national public procurement platform, Government e-Marketplace (GeM) has achieved a cumulative Gross Merchandise Value of over 20 lakh crore rupees in the last ten years. GeM was launched on 9th August 2016 to transform public procurement through technology, transparency, efficiency and good governance. Addressing a press conference in New Delhi, GeM CEO Mihir Kumar said that the GeMs  business has grown from 422 crore rupees in 2016-17 to over 20 lakh crore rupees now. He said that over the past decade, GeM has emerged as a cornerstone of India’s digital governance ecosystem.Mr Kumar informed that according to a study done by IIT Delhi, the items sold on GeM was cheaper on 74 per cent items in comparison with other e marketplace like Amazon, Flipkart and India Mart. He said, the sellers on GeM platform have grown from around three thousand to over 25 lakh, while the Micro and Small Enterprises registered on the platform have also risen from around two thousand to more than 12 lakh.    Mr Kumar said that today all States are onboarded on GeM platform and soon it will reach out to Urban Local Bodies and Gram Panchayats to expand its business.
. In the forex market today, the rupee depreciated by 10 paise to end at 95 rupees and 22 paise against the US dollar.

. India has called for safe and unimpeded navigation and free flow of commerce through international waterways as it attached high priority to safety and security of Indian vessels and seafarers. Briefing media in New Delhi today, External Affairs Ministry Spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said Indian Missions all across the Gulf region are in constant contact with the Ministry of Shipping and maritime authorities in those countries. He said, 24/7 helplines are being run so that any person who needs support can also approach them. The helplines are operating all throughout last several months. New Delhi has also called upon all parties to refrain from targeting civilian infrastructure and civilian vessels and seafarers.On the question of the US lawmaker’s objection on the proposed Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Amendment Bill, Mr Jaiswal said  India has rejected the objections saying that its legislative matters are its internal affairs in which the decisions are taken by the Parliament. Mr Jaiswal pointed out that there are several nations including the US which regulate the flow of foreign funds.Replying to a question on the press conference of former Prime Minister of Bangladesh Sheikh Hasina, Mr Jaiswal reiterated that India had no role to playOn last night’s telephonic conversation between Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, the MEA spokesperson said both leaders discussed the ongoing situation and developments in West Asia. He added that the call was made from the Israeli side. He added that India has Special Strategic Partnership with the country. The spokesperson said that during the conversation between the two leaders, strengthening the cooperation across various sectors was discussed.Replying to the defence pact between Pakistan, Turkey and Saudi Arabia, the spokesperson said the development is being closely followed. On recent defence pact between Pakistan and Somalia, Mr Jaiswal said, India continues to follow these developments closely.The spokesperson said, India is looking forward to organising India Africa Forum Summit.  Both sides are in touch with each other for a convenient date as to when it can be organised.

. The Government has said that 60 merchant vessels carrying cargo were safely moved through the Strait of Hormuz despite the heightened security situation in the West Asia region. Replying to a question in Parliament, the government also disclosed that 3,972 Indian seafarers were repatriated from the Gulf region, while a round-the-clock crisis management system handled tens of thousands of distress calls and emails.The government’s response highlights India’s maritime response during the ongoing West Asia crisis, underscoring how New Delhi managed to keep one of the country’s most critical trade arteries functioning even as tensions threatened shipping through the Strait of Hormuz. The strategic waterway connects the Persian Gulf to the Gulf of Oman and the Arabian Sea, and serves as the world’s most critical maritime chokepoint for energy supplies.

. India’s Ambassador to Japan, Nagma Mallick, today laid flowers at the Hiroshima Peace Memorial Park and paid tribute to the victims of the atomic bomb. The Indian envoy’s visit to Hiroshima came as the city marked the 81st anniversary of the US atomic bombing.Ambassador Mallick met Hiroshima Governor Mika Yokota and Hiroshima Mayor Kazumi Matsui at a reception where the diplomatic corps in Japan were invited to attend the Hiroshima Peace Memorial Ceremony.On August 6, 1945, a uranium bomb, carried aboard US bomber Enola Gay, was detonated over Hiroshima in the final stages of the Second World War, killing an estimated 140,000 people. Approximately 50,000 people gathered at Peace Memorial Park to pay tribute to the victims of the atomic bomb. Representatives of 121 nations and the European Union participated in the ceremony held at Hiroshima Peace Memorial Park.

. Union Culture Minister Gajendra Singh Shekhawat today said that saree is not merely a piece of attire, rather a magnificent symbol of Indian culture. The Minister said this in a video message during Saree Shastra in New Delhi. Mr Shekhawat underlined the mastery of wearing one saree in multiple ways, the craft of designing and weaving a single saree in diverse styles. Highlighting the tradition of representing culture through sarees, he said that exhibitions and events like this help spread awareness about India’s tradition of wearing and weaving sarees, and understanding which saree suits which occasion far and wide.Minister of State for Youth Affairs and Sports Raksha Khadse said that the exhibition serves as a prime example of presenting diverse states and culture through sarees. The Minister said that the exhibition brings together artists from across the country and aims to present their work through the medium of the saree. He said, it reflects the country’s rich culture, which is being conveyed through saree craftsmanship.Saree Shastra is a three-day exhibition to honour the women who weave, preserve and wear sarees. The event reimangines the saree as one of India’s most enduring cultural artefact.

. The two-day BRICS WAVES Bazaar, a premier international marketplace for the creative economy began in Mumbai today. The event, being held under India’s BRICS Presidency brings together over 500 delegates from BRICS members and partners from 21 countries with an aim to create stronger pathways for collaboration across film, television, animation, VFX, gaming, music, digital media and emerging content formats.Information and Broadcasting Secretary, Mr. Chanchal Kumar said WAVES Bazaar seeks to become a platform for the global creative economy where projects are discovered, partnerships are initiated, co-productions are discussed and new markets are opened. Delivering the keynote address in the opening ceremony, Maharashtra’s Minister of Electronics, IT, AI and Culture, Adv. Ashish Shelar said the BRICS WAVES Bazaar is a high-level, curated confluence designed to shape the future of the global creative economy. Union Minister for Youth Affairs and Sports Dr Mansukh Mandaviya today felicitated Indian athletes who returned from the Commonwealth Games 2026 after delivering historic performances in boxing, judo and para-athletics. During the felicitation ceremony held in New Delhi, the medal winners were presented cash awards of 30 lakh rupees for gold, 20 lakh rupees for silver and 10 lakh rupees for bronze.Interacting with the athletes, Dr. Mandaviya asked the athletes to think beyond their playing careers and become contributors to the next generation of Indian sport. The Minister highlighted the revamped Khelo India scheme of worth rupees 36,000 crore. He said that this initiative will take care of greater continued investment in the growth of Indian sports in the coming years. Congratulating the champions, Dr. Mandaviya urged them to extend their contribution to Indian sport beyond their competitive careers by mentoring and inspiring the next generation of athletes.

. At the World Athletics Under 20 Championships, India’s Mohammed Ashfaq broke the Under 20 national record in Eugene, United States today. With this win, Ashfaq paved his way to qualify for the men’s 400 metre semifinals. The 19-year-old Ashfaq clocked 45.81 seconds to finish second behind USA’s Jayden DeLeon in the first round heat 5 and fourth overall to make it to the semifinals.In the men’s high jump, India’s Basant qualified for the final with a jump of 2.14 metre, finishing fifth in qualification Group A. India’s Amanat Kamboj finished sixth in women’s discus throw finals with a personal best effort. He bettered his own previous national record of 46.05 seconds, set earlier this season in April.

India has rejected the objections raised by a US lawmaker on the proposed Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Amendment Bill saying that its legislative matters are its internal affairs in which the decisions are taken by the Parliament. External Affairs Ministry Spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said this during a media briefing in New Delhi while replying to a question in this regard. Mr Jaiswal pointed out that there are several nations, including the US, which regulate the flow of foreign funds.On safety and security of Indian vessels and seafarers, Mr Jaiswal said, New Delhi attaches high priority to the issue. He said, Indian Missions all across the Gulf region are in constant contact with the Ministry of Shipping and maritime authorities in those countries. He said, 24/7 helplines are being run so that any person who needs support can also approach them. He said, India continues to call for safe and unimpeded navigation and free flow of commerce through international waterways. New Delhi has also called upon all parties to refrain from targeting civilian infrastructure and civilian vessels and seafarers.Replying to the defence pact between Pakistan, Turkey and Saudi Arabia, the spokesperson said the development is being closely followed. On recent defence pact between Pakistan and Somalia, Mr Jaiswal said, India continues to follow these developments closely.

The National Stock Exchange (NSE) has proposed a stricter regulatory framework for Authorised Persons (APs) to strengthen investor protection, improve supervision and enhance accountability of stockbrokers. The proposals have been issued through a consultation paper prepared jointly by stock exchanges in consultation with the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI). Public comments have been invited till 27th of this month.Under the proposed framework, individual Authorised Persons will be required to maintain a minimum net worth of five lakh rupees, while partnership firms, LLPs and body corporates will need a minimum net worth of 25 lakh rupees.The proposals also mandate disclosure of all banks and demat accounts, business-related websites and social media handles, besides technology-based safeguards such as geo-tagging, CCTV surveillance and biometric authentication at trading terminals. Stockbrokers will be responsible for the acts of their Authorised Persons and will be required to conduct regular inspections, surprise audits and enhanced monitoring to safeguard investors.

. Parliament has passed the Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises Development (Amendment) Bill 2026, with the Lok Sabha approving it today. Rajya Sabha had passed the bill on Monday.When the House met after the first adjournment at 12 noon, Minister of MSME Jitan Ram Manjhi moved the bill to further amend the Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises Development Act, 2006. The Bill aims to address payment delays and simplify dispute resolution.The legislation provides that every central public sector enterprise must settle all invoices for procurement of goods or services from MSMEs on the Trade Receivables Discounting System. As per the bill, if mediation fails in case of dispute, then the reference for arbitration must be made within 30 days from the date of termination of mediation. It also adds that an award must be made within 90 days from the date of completion of pleadings. The Bill provides that if a case has been pending for more than six months, at least 50 per cent of the awarded amount must be paid to the supplier.After passing the Bill, the Presiding Officer Dilip Saikia tried to run the House and appealed to the protesting members to allow the House to function. He expressed displeasure over the disruptions, stating that such protests are not appropriate for the country’s democratic system. Mr Saikia said that repeatedly bringing posters and banners and obstructing the proceedings is not right as it hampers the functioning of the House.The Presiding Officer urged the members to go back to their seats and engage in constructive dialogue, adding that they would be given full opportunity to raise their issues. He reiterated that maintaining the dignity of the House is the responsibility of all members and proceedings must be conducted smoothly.Parliamentary Affairs Minister Kiren Rijiju expressed concern over the opposition’s conduct, saying that Union Home Minister Amit Shah always comes to Parliament during the session and remains present till late night.As the uproar continued, the Presiding Officer adjourned the House for the day to meet again at 11:00 AM on Monday. Earlier, when the House met at 11 AM, Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla paid tributes to the freedom fighters and martyrs of the Quit India Movement. He said that 9th August marks the 84th anniversary of the Quit India Movement.Recalling Mahatma Gandhi’s historic call of Do or Die, Mr Birla described the movement as an enduring symbol of national unity, courage, truth and non-violence. He said, it also reaffirmed the nation’s commitment to democracy, freedom, national unity and the values enshrined in the Constitution. The Speaker said that this movement paved the way for a decisive mass awakening towards achieving independence and infused new energy into the nation’s self-confidence.The House also paid its tribute to the Father of the Nation, Mahatma Gandhi, and to the freedom fighters and martyrs who made the supreme sacrifice for the country’s independence. The House also observed silence in honour of the freedom fighters and martyrs.After that, Mr Birla tried to take up the Question Hour, but the opposition members raised the issue of alleged police action during students’ protests. The opposition members were demanding a statement from Union Home Minister Amit Shah on alleged police action during students’ protests.The Speaker said, Question Hour is an important part of the proceedings, which provides every member an opportunity to raise issues. Mr Birla added that Parliament is meant for discussion, for raising questions, and for meaningful exchange of ideas. As the pandemonium continued, the Lok Sabha was adjourned till 12:00 noon.

. Widening use of security powers by Pakistani forces has increased human rights concerns in Pakistan-occupied Jammu and Kashmir, PoJK. Over the past decade, the Office of the United Nations High Commissioner for Human Rights and several other international organisations have repeatedly raised concerns over enforced disappearances, excessive use of force, restrictions on freedom of expression, and lack of accountability in the occupied territory. On July 27, the first day of so-called legislative elections in PoJK, violent clashes broke out in Rawalakot, with the Joint Awami Action Committee (JAAC) alleging that Pakistani security forces used live ammunition against protesters, resulting in several deaths and injuries.A report in Brussels-based EU Reporter has highlighted that the ongoing shutdown of mobile and internet services made independent verification difficult, restricting the ability of journalists and human rights groups to assess the situation on the ground. According to the report, counterterrorism laws and emergency measures are increasingly being applied to manage routine political dissent in the PoJK.

The Government today said India has been advocating for early commencement of text-based negotiations with clearly laid out timelines and milestones regarding permanent membership for India in an expanded United Nations Security Council (UNSC). In a written reply in Lok Sabha, Minister of State for External Affairs Kirti Vardhan Singh today said that India consistently highlights the need for expanding both permanent and non-permanent categories in UNSC and greater representation of the developing countries, with emphasis on the Global South.The External Affairs Ministry has taken up the matter of permanent membership for India both bilaterally and multilaterally at various levels, including at the highest levels. The MoS said that Ministry’s engagements in this regard cover various countries, including all five permanent members of the UNSC. Mr Singh said that the government strongly believes that India has all the credentials to be a permanent member of a reformed and expanded UNSC that reflects contemporary global realities.
